$comment: The authoritative package catalog: one entry per workspace package, giving it
exactly one role, an explicit dependency contract, and an explicit statement of
what it must never do.
Why this exists
The dependency direction was already correct and already enforced -- but only
pairwise, by hand-written rules in tools/validate-boundaries.mjs section 10
('application must not import cli', 'mcp must not import cli', ...). Adding a
package meant remembering to hand-write its rules, and nothing said what a
package was FOR. Three properties were therefore unenforced: no cycle check, no
general rule that a layer may only depend downward, and no guard against
importing another package's internals.
This catalog states those properties as data. tools/validate-packages.mjs
derives the checks from it, so the guarantees hold for every package including
ones added later.
IMPORTANT: this file does not describe a repair. The v0.5.4 audit found the
graph already cycle-free, no cross-package deep `src/` imports anywhere, and
@oh-my-pm/contracts already dependency-free. The catalog LOCKS IN that
structure; it did not create it.
Fields, per entry:
role          the single architectural role. Layer order is the `layers`
array below: a package may depend only on its own layer or a
LOWER one, which is what makes the direction mechanical
rather than a list of pairs.
allowed       workspace packages this package may declare as production
dependencies. Anything outside this set is a violation even if
the layer order would permit it, so a package cannot quietly
widen its surface.
forbidden     packages this package must never depend on OR import, called
out explicitly because these are the inversions that would
break the architecture rather than merely surprise a reader.
sideEffects   which process-level effects the package may perform.
`stdout`/`stderr`/`exit` are reserved for presentation and
executable boundaries; a package below the presentation
layer writing to a stream makes it unusable by a second
surface.
inBundle      whether the release bundler deploys this package's code.
Verified against a real built bundle, not assumed.
dataOwnership what state the package is authoritative for; `none` means it
owns no persistent state.
testOwnership where the package's behaviour is verified.
$layerComment: Ordered lowest to highest. A package may depend on its own layer or any
layer to its LEFT, never to its right. `development` is highest so nothing
can depend on it.
These names describe THIS graph rather than importing a generic
domain/infrastructure split, which does not fit: `providers` owns both the
network boundary and the ProviderRegistry abstraction that `planner` is
written against, so neither is cleanly 'above' the other under the usual
convention. Ranking by actual longest dependency path gives an unambiguous
order, and each name states the job of that rank:
contract       shared shapes and owned local state, no workspace deps
(contracts, project-memory)
capability     a single self-contained capability over the contracts
(kernel, providers, skills)
composition    combines capabilities without orchestrating a request
(planner, installer)
orchestration  sequences capabilities into a request/response flow
(runtime)
application    the shared use cases every surface consumes (application)
presentation   an adapter over the application boundary (cli, mcp-server)
packaging      the release dependency surface and entrypoints
(distribution)
development    harnesses that ship no code (examples)
`project-memory` sits at `contract` because it declares no workspace
dependency at all: it owns the store format the way contracts owns the
shared shapes. `kernel` is a capability, not infrastructure -- it is the
pure Rust/WASM control plane, and WASM instantiation is an implementation
detail of that same package.

packages.name: @oh-my-pm/contracts
responsibilities: own the shared data shapes for the whole workspace
own the generated TypeScript and Rust contract output
own the schema that both generated forms derive from
nonResponsibilities: know any provider, runtime, or presentation concept
packages.compatibility: generated contract shapes and their schemaVersion values

packages.name: @oh-my-pm/project-memory
responsibilities: own the local Project Brain record store format
own snapshot capture, comparison, and chronology semantics
own the store-format version and its migration rules
packages.dataOwnership: the local Project Memory store (store format 2)
packages.compatibility: store format version and record envelope shapes

packages.name: @oh-my-pm/kernel
responsibilities: expose the pure Rust/WASM control plane to TypeScript
own validation, state, feature-flag, and update-safety decisions
own the generated WASM binding surface
nonResponsibilities: know a provider or a presentation surface
packages.compatibility: kernel API surface and the Rust crate version
packages.testOwnership: kernel/binding/test plus the Rust crate's own tests

packages.name: @oh-my-pm/providers
responsibilities: own read-only context acquisition from local and GitHub sources
own the single GitHub network boundary (github/transport.ts)
normalize provider items into the shared shape
packages.compatibility: provider identifiers, normalized item shape, and config schema

packages.name: @oh-my-pm/skills
responsibilities: own deterministic project-management transformations
own the skill registry and its envelopes
nonResponsibilities: depend on wall-clock time or randomness

packages.name: @oh-my-pm/planner
responsibilities: own task planning and dependency shaping over provider items

packages.name: @oh-my-pm/runtime
responsibilities: own request orchestration and execution flow
sequence Kernel validation, provider acquisition, planning, and skills
produce a RuntimeResponse
$devDependencyComment: @oh-my-pm/project-memory is a DEV dependency only: the runtime's
project_changes tests exercise real store fixtures, while the runtime
itself must not import the store. The boundary validator asserts the
production direction, so this dev edge cannot become a runtime one.

packages.name: @oh-my-pm/application
responsibilities: own the shared use cases every presentation surface consumes
own workflow sequencing, failure classification, and result contracts
own the presentation-neutral response projection
nonResponsibilities: write to a stream or choose an exit code
know an executable name, an MCP tool, or a terminal output mode
packages.compatibility: ApplicationResult, Diagnostic, error taxonomy, and use-case signatures

packages.name: @oh-my-pm/installer
responsibilities: own the deterministic installation and update lifecycle
own manifest validation, install/update/rollback planning and reports
own real transactional installation into an explicit prefix
nonResponsibilities: download an artifact or make any network request
edit PATH, a shell profile, or an MCP client configuration
packages.dataOwnership: the installed prefix layout and install.json
packages.compatibility: install manifest shape and installed layout

packages.name: @oh-my-pm/cli
responsibilities: own the command grammar, parsing, and help
own terminal formatting, output-mode selection, and stream routing
own the CLI exit-code mapping
compose the local runtime identity for the status/doctor/plan commands
nonResponsibilities: own shared business logic any other surface needs
be imported by another presentation surface
packages.compatibility: command surface, flags, output formats, and exit codes
$asymmetryComment: The CLI declares runtime/providers/skills/kernel while the MCP server
reaches the shared project workflows through @oh-my-pm/application. That
is INTENTIONAL, not residual duplication: cli/src/local-process.ts
composes a local Runtime for `status`, `doctor`, and `plan`, which are
runtime-identity and free-form planning commands the application boundary
does not expose and that no second surface consumes. The four SHARED
project workflows (brief/risks/next/handoff) go through the application
boundary on both surfaces, and tests/e2e asserts they agree semantically.
Until v0.6.1 that last sentence was aspirational: the CLI called only the
shared document loader and then re-composed the Runtime, provider, and
Kernel itself, so the two surfaces shared one step of the pipeline rather
than all of it. The CLI now calls runLocalProjectWorkflow directly, and
tools/validate-application-boundary.mjs fails if either half of the claim
stops holding -- a shared workflow re-composed per surface, or a CLI-only
command pushed through the boundary for symmetry alone.
@oh-my-pm/project-memory is a production dependency so it ships in the
bundle, while being reached only through a lazy dynamic import;

packages.name: @oh-my-pm/mcp-server
responsibilities: own MCP tool registration, input schemas, and annotations
own strict source projection and structured content
own protocol stdout safety and the MCP error mapping
nonResponsibilities: own shared business logic any other surface needs
expose an HTTP or SSE transport
packages.compatibility: MCP tool inventory, order, input schemas, and annotations

packages.name: @oh-my-pm/distribution
responsibilities: declare the production dependency surface the release bundler deploys
provide the thin portable command entrypoints, canonical and alias
nonResponsibilities: contain build logic or a repository path
become a dependency of any domain or application package
write files or reach the network
$inBundleComment: The bundle IS this package's entrypoints plus the deployed dependency
tree, so it is not itself a nested node_modules entry. Verified against a
real built bundle: node_modules/@oh-my-pm contains the eleven deployed
packages, and distribution is not among them.
packages.compatibility: installed command names and entrypoint paths
packages.testOwnership: distribution/libexec plus the release qualification tooling

packages.name: @oh-my-pm/examples
responsibilities: wire the real packages together so each documented composition is tested
own the Markdown project fixtures the installed qualification analyzes
nonResponsibilities: be imported by any shipped package
contribute to the release dependency graph
be the only place a behaviour is verified
